doc.title: Ben Sidran interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 15, 2023

title: Titles, music first, and Jon Hendricks on writing words
summary: He always writes music first; Hendricks said the music tells you the story.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Do you have a title in mind before you start most of your songs?

That’s a good question. I often do. I often do. On the other hand a lot of times the title will emerge when some phrase becomes repetitive and you realize oh, well there’s the title. Everything I write I have to say starts music first. I’ve never written something out that looks like a poem and then tried to put music to it. It always comes from sitting at the piano playing something. And Jon Hendricks, the great lyricist, told me that a lot of people think that what he does is fit words into a musical setting. He said, “Like a jeweler would put gems in a setting.” He said, “But that’s not it at all.” He said, “The way I write words is I listen to the music over and over until the music starts talking. The music tells you the story.”

Oh that’s terrific. I had the privilege of talking to him and he also said that sometimes he got — when he was doing “Sing a Song of Basie” he said he was watching his hand write out the words like he was getting this —
